title: complete noobie not sure where to start

posts.author: TwilightOcean
posts.body:
I'm mostly a noobie, but I used to fool around with earlier versions of RPG maker when I was a young kid for hours all day but the scripts and codes never really worked on my end for some reason, but I am new to the whole concept of "plugins" being a thing, it sounds a lot easier. But that being said, I am familiar with the basics of the programs somewhat. I really want to make a superhero themed RPG, I want to make a Zelda styled game but turn based instead of action RPG, I just planned on using the game play mechanics for the puzzle solving mostly, particularly all the tools. Since Zelda is well established, and I don't plan to deviate from the basics too much, it should be easy to accomplish this, shouldn't it?
I plan to make most of the graphics and sprites on my own since I feel underwhelmed by most of the ones which are available. Just wondering if there are more experiences users who know where on the interwebs to go, and what I need to know. I tried looking up "zelda plugins" and ended up here. There is a vast array of sites, but they seem difficult to navigate and not all too concise. I am really excited and want to start working on the game right away. I am honestly just used to looking at websites with tons of codes, and looking for codes for hours and then not having them work out.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
It's difficult to guess your level of experience from your post, so I'll start with the basics:
the last two makers had build-in tutorials under the help-menu that might be worth your time to work through to refresh everything.
if you haven't done so, please go through everything in the editor, clicking on every button to see what is behind it. That means both database and event structure as well as mapping options.
The reason is that MZ has added a lot of small additions and optimisations for many event commands and deep options like the game data part of control variable or others. Even experienced users of older makers have to find them on their own because there never was a full list of all the changes (or I haven't seen it if there is).
One change is especially hidden: go to database, animations, select an empty animation slot and right-click its ID, then select MV-compatible data to get the old animation definitions.
Additionally, my old "starting point" tutorial (see signature) is still valid even for MZ aside from some minor changes.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
In addition to doing the built-in tutorial and thoroughly going through MZ itself to explore all the options available, I'd also suggest the following, before jumping down the rabbit hole of getting a bunch of plugins:
In MZ, go to the tab for Help and then select Contents to read a fairly helpful reference document. You will probably want to refer back to that.
Search YouTube for some tutorial series for MZ that go from the basics to more advanced concepts. Don't just watch these tutorials. Recreate them in your own sample project and do additional experiments with things as they catch your interest. You can find some good comprehensive tutorial series. They are older and a few things have changed, but the majority of the content is still relevant and valuable.
After you have a fairly good grasp of what is available in the database, the Event Command options, etc., check out the default plugins that come with MZ. I am particularly fond of the TextPicture and ButtonPicture plugins. I use those a lot.
Start experimenting with mechanics, concepts, and ideas that interest you and you are curious about in your sample project. This can really help you learn more.
Consider learning some Javascript by using an online course like W3Schools or a book. There are multiple places in MZ where you can directly insert Scripts (Javascript) and there is a TON that you can do with that. There is a very nice RPG Maker MV_MZ Script Calls excel spreadsheet that is very helpful once you learn a little Javascript.
Try making a very small game with what you have learned so you can experience the end to end process and work out problems.
Once you have a good, solid foundation, then you will probably be better equipped to figure out what (if any) plugins you really need to make the game you want.
Anyway, these are just some suggestions from an older user who didn't discover RPG Maker until about 4 years ago. I learned mostly from recreating tutorials in the beginning and then just experimenting and exploring things that interested me. I had no real programming experience, but I have found that learning MZ and Javascript really isn't that difficult if you are willing to put in the time and effort.
Good luck on your projects and always feel free to ask questions when you need to. Remember to enjoy what you do!
